title: How much cake does each friend get?
description: A cake is mostly eaten, and the part that is left is shared equally among three friends. The part left comes from taking four fifths from one whole, and the sharing is done with the reciprocal of three.
teaching_notes: One idea: find the part of the cake that is left, then share that part, not the whole cake. Watch for students who divide the whole cake by three, or who share the four fifths.

source: Figure it Out (problems with fractions): a grandmother baked a cake. A girl and her cousins finished 4/5 of the cake. The remaining cake was shared equally by the girl's three friends. How much of the cake did each friend get?
video_script.why: A learner finds the part left from one whole, then shares it equally by multiplying with the reciprocal, as with the milk in the cups of tea.
video_script.substitution: the book's own cake, with four fifths eaten and the rest shared among three friends
video_script.anchor: a cake cut into five equal slices, with four slices eaten and one slice left
video_script.payoff_line: Each friend gets one fifteenth of the whole cake.

final_answer.spoken: one fifteenth of the whole cake

video_script.fraction_reading: four fifths, one fifth, one third, one fifteenth, three fifteenths
video_script.design: A whole cake in five slices; four are crossed out and the last slice is cut into three equal pieces.
